quizzes.title: Sanctioning Russia Act: Scope and Review
quizzes.passage:
The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 is a law that the United States has enacted. The measure followed Senate approval and House passage, and it was then signed by the President. Its main aim is to increase economic pressure on Russia, and it also extends and strengthens certain sanctions against Iran. The Act targets political, financial, energy and commercial networks linked to Russia's war in Ukraine. It is now federal law with greater legal permanence.

The Act's criteria bring major buyers of Russian oil and gas within its scope. India is one such buyer because it remains one of the major buyers of Russian crude. Tariffs under the Act can fall on the largest purchasers of Russian energy and on facilitators of Russian oil sanctions evasion. Certain goods of Russian origin may also face tariffs, subject to specified exceptions.

The list of relevant purchasers is not fixed. It is reviewed periodically, in consultation with other senior officials. Countries that import only a small share of their natural gas from Russia can qualify for an exception if they take significant steps to reduce such imports. The sanctions framework may also be affected if certain conditions relating to the war are met.

questions.q: Under the Act, which of the following conditions could affect the sanctions framework?
options: Russia expands its energy exports to Asia
Russia joins the World Trade Organization
questions.explanation: The Act lists ceasing military hostilities among the conditions that may affect the framework.

questions.q: Which body must review the list of major Russian oil and gas importers?
questions.explanation: The USTR, consulting the Secretaries of State and Energy, must review that list.

questions.q: What review cycle does the Act provide for reassessing relevant purchasers?
questions.explanation: The Act provides a 180-day review cycle for relevant purchasers.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Act names India and China directly as countries subject to its tariffs.
Reason (R): Its criteria place major buyers like India and China within its regulatory scope.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The Act names no individual nations, although its criteria cover major buyers such as India and China.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Iran Sanctions Act extension (year)   ->   A. 15%
II. Natural gas import share for exception   ->   B. 500%
III. Tariff on Russian-origin goods (maximum)   ->   C. 5
IV. Largest purchasers facing tariffs (number)   ->   D. 2031
questions.explanation: The Iran extension runs to 2031, the natural gas threshold is 15%, the Russian-origin goods tariff is up to 500%, and five largest purchasers are covered.

questions.q:
Consider the statements below about the sanctions framework:
I. The President signed the Act into law on 18 September 2026.
II. The Act names India directly as a country subject to its tariffs.
III. Russia ending activities aimed at undermining the Ukrainian Government is one condition for ending the framework.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the Act names no individual nations.

questions.q:
Read the statements below about the Act.
I. The House of Representatives passed the legislation by 262 votes to 159.
II. The Act sets a 30-day review cycle for relevant purchasers.
III. The Act authorises tariffs of up to 100% on the largest purchasers of Russian oil and gas.
How many of these statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the review cycle is 180 days.

quizzes.title: Sanctioning Russia Act: Key Figures
quizzes.passage:
A law named the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 has been enacted in the United States. The measure followed Senate approval and passage in the House of Representatives, and the President then signed it into law. Its main objective is to increase economic pressure on Russia over the war in Ukraine. The Act also extends and strengthens certain sanctions against Iran.

The Act sets out a wide-ranging package aimed at political, financial, energy and commercial networks that help sustain Russia's war. Although it does not single out nations, its criteria place major buyers of Russian oil and gas within scope. India is affected because it remains one of the major buyers of Russian crude. Tariffs can be imposed on the largest purchasers of Russian energy, and on facilitators of Russian oil sanctions evasion.

Relevant purchasers are reassessed at intervals, with the review involving other senior officials. The Act also allows exceptions for countries that import a small share of natural gas from Russia and take significant steps to reduce such imports. The sanctions can be affected if Russia meets conditions tied to ending the war, as set out in the law. The Act is now federal law, which gives it greater legal permanence.

questions.q: How many days is the review cycle for reassessing relevant purchasers? (number of days)
questions.explanation: The Act provides a 180-day review cycle for relevant purchasers.

questions.q: Through which year does the Act extend the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996? (year)
questions.explanation: The Act extends the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 through 2031.

questions.q: Below what percentage share of natural gas imports from Russia can a country qualify for the exception? (per cent)
questions.explanation: A country importing less than 15% of its natural gas from Russia can qualify for the exception if it takes significant steps to reduce imports.

questions.q: How many of the largest purchasers of Russian oil and gas can face tariffs under the Act? (number)
questions.explanation: The Act authorises tariffs on the 5 largest purchasers of Russian oil and natural gas.

questions.q: Which word qualifies the name of the sanctions structure that the Act sets up? (one word)
questions.explanation: The Act sets up a Comprehensive Sanctions Framework covering political, financial, energy and commercial networks.

questions.q: How many House members voted in favour of the legislation? (number)
questions.explanation: The House passed the legislation 262 to 159 on 16 September.

questions.q: On which day of September 2026 was the Act signed into law? (day of month)
questions.explanation: The President signed the Act into law on 18 September 2026.

quizzes.title: Sanctions Act: India and Global Oil
quizzes.passage:
The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 was enacted by the United States in September 2026. The Act is aimed mainly at economic pressure on Russia over the war in Ukraine, and it also strengthens certain sanctions against Iran. Its criteria place major buyers of Russian energy within its scope. The measure was passed by Congress and signed into federal law, which gives it greater legal permanence. It follows an earlier punitive tariff on India for buying Russian oil. The authorisation covers tariffs on major purchasers of Russian oil and natural gas.

India remains one of the major buyers of Russian crude, so the measure matters for India's energy planning. Russia is a major source of India's oil, and the country depends on imports to meet a large part of its energy demand. This makes the measure significant for India.

The measure reflects a broader pattern in which tariffs and sanctions are used to shape the conduct of other countries. Crude oil is traded in a connected global market.

Russia's war in Ukraine remains the central context for the measure. Indian policymakers face a difficult set of choices. They must weigh their relationships with the United States, Russia and other major powers while protecting national energy interests.

questions.q: According to the booklet, what could major buyers do before potential tariff measures take effect?
options: Stop all purchases of Russian crude
Increase purchases before potential tariff measures
Shift all shipments to a single supplier
questions.explanation: The booklet says major buyers may increase purchases before potential tariff measures.

questions.q: Removing substantial Russian crude from global markets could place additional pressure on what, if alternative supplies are insufficient?
questions.explanation: The booklet links removal of substantial Russian crude to additional pressure on international oil prices when alternative supplies fall short.

questions.q: Discounted crude improves buyers' economics, but replacing large volumes of it is challenging in which respect?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes replacing large volumes of discounted crude as logistically challenging.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Higher import bills can raise the cost of transport and manufacturing.
Reason (R): Higher import bills drive up transport, logistics, manufacturing and consumer prices.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and the reason directly explains the effect on transport and manufacturing costs.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Discounted crude   ->   A. Complicates India-U.S. bilateral trade
II. Replacing large volumes of crude   ->   B. Logistically challenging
III. Potential tariffs   ->   C. Improves buyers' economics
IV. Energy contracts of major buyers   ->   D. Reconfigured by major buyers
questions.explanation: Discounted crude improves economics, replacing volumes is logistically challenging, tariffs complicate bilateral trade, and buyers reconfigure energy contracts.

questions.q:
Consider the statements below about how major buyers may respond:
I. Buyers may develop alternative payment and logistics arrangements.
II. Replacing large volumes of discounted crude is logistically easy.
III. Buyers may reconfigure energy contracts.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the booklet calls replacing large volumes logistically challenging.

questions.q:
Read the statements below and choose the option giving the number of correct statements.
I. Discounted crude improves the economics for buyers.
II. Replacing large volumes of Russian crude is logistically easy.
III. Major buyers may diversify their suppliers.
How many of these statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because replacing large volumes is logistically challenging.

quizzes.title: Sanctions Act: Buyers and Markets
quizzes.passage:
The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 is a recent measure from the United States. It targets economic pressure on Russia over the war in Ukraine and strengthens certain sanctions against Iran. The Act's criteria place major buyers of Russian energy within its scope.

India is one of the major buyers of Russian crude, which makes the measure relevant for its energy planning. Russia is a major source of the oil India imports, and India relies on imports to meet a large share of demand. The new law also follows an earlier punitive tariff that was imposed on India for buying Russian oil.

The Act reflects a wider approach in which tariffs and sanctions are used to shape the conduct of other countries. Crude oil moves through one connected global market, so a sizeable fall in Russian supply would reach other buyers as well. The Act was signed into federal law, which gives it greater legal permanence than the earlier tariff.

Indian policymakers must weigh relationships with the United States, Russia and other major powers. At the same time, they must protect national energy interests. Russia's war in Ukraine remains the central context for the entire measure. The Act also provides exceptions for certain purchasers.

questions.q: What type of crude oil improves buyers' economics but is harder to replace in large volumes? (two words)
questions.explanation: Discounted crude improves economics, though replacing large volumes is logistically challenging.

questions.q: What term does the booklet use for India's balancing of relationships with major powers and national energy interests? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet frames this balance under the heading Navigating Strategic Autonomy.

questions.q: What kind of agreements may major buyers reconfigure in response? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says major buyers may reconfigure energy contracts.

questions.q: What may major buyers do with their supplier base? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says major buyers may diversify suppliers.

questions.q: If alternative supplies are insufficient, removing substantial Russian crude from global markets could add pressure on which measure? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says removing substantial Russian crude could place additional pressure on international oil prices.

questions.q: What challenge does replacing large volumes of discounted crude present? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes replacing large volumes as logistically challenging.

questions.q: What may major buyers do before potential tariff measures take effect? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says buyers may increase purchases before potential tariff measures.
